prize_parts.citation: for showing how technological change and trade exposure reshape labour demand, wage structure and local labour-market adjustment

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B006 with Autor, Hanson and Katz as a single prize part. What changed is how I hold it. The chair rightly warns that ten of eleven round-1 files converge on the same trio, and that this is not evidence of merit. So I asked whether I would still choose B006 if no colleague had. I think I would, on three grounds. (1) Question and framework: the work asks who bears the cost of technological and trade-driven change, and pairs a conceptual account (skill demand, tasks, the race between education and technology) with design-based local-labour-market evidence. (2) Maturity: the core papers run from the early 1990s to the mid-2010s, so there has been a long period of replication, extension to other countries and sustained critique. The live disputes concern the magnitude and persistence of effects, not whether they exist. (3) Fit with my own field: as an economic historian of electrification and regional change, I see the same pattern in the historical record, with uneven adjustment across places that aggregates hide and costs that can be lasting. This is a field proximity I disclose and have tried to hold to the common criteria. On the chair's Katz-versus-Dorn question, I keep Katz because the citation then covers the long-run skill-demand and wage-structure account that gives the trade-shock evidence its interpretive frame. A Dorn variant would be a cleaner trade-shock prize but a narrower one. I would not support a two-name Autor-Hanson prize, since it would drop the skill-premium strand while still leaving Dorn out. On drafting, I propose one citation that treats this as one question (how technology and trade shift labour demand and where adjustment costs fall), makes no claim to have originated the task framework, and states no settled long-run magnitude. On the shift-share and persistence debate, the established finding (effects on labour demand and local adjustment) is sufficient for the prize. The committee should not treat the headline magnitudes as settled.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakest part, and Katz is the most contestable name in my configuration. Dorn is a central co-author of the China-shock papers and is excluded by the three-name cap. Levy and Murnane, and Acemoglu's task-model theory, lie outside the credited names. Katz's best-known education-technology work was done with a recent laureate, so his marginal credit overlaps with the 2023 prize, and I cannot show from the supplied evidence how much of his wage-structure work is separable from that. A reader could also see two adjacent lines, technology and trade, joined by a shared outcome rather than one discovery. Persistence, external validity and shift-share inference remain debated. B007 has cleaner attribution and B001 has broad reach, so a committee that weights separable credit above breadth could reasonably prefer either.

responses.point: Friberg prefers B007 and ranks B006 sixth. He would credit only Autor and Hanson. He reads B006 as two related lines and wants credit and citation settled before treating it as one clean discovery.
responses.response: I accept the two-lines reading as a real description of the credit. I disagree that it favours a pair. Autor and Hanson alone credit the trade-shock and task evidence, and Katz is the name tied to the long-run skill-premium account that frames it. I also accept that Katz's overlap with the 2023 prize calls for careful wording, not silence. I can draft the citation around labour demand and adjustment, so the two lines become one question. On B007, I share your view that its credit is cleaner and that the theory and state-capacity work are its strongest parts. For me the gap is identification of the cross-country constitutional and electoral-rule results, and that is a scientific reservation, not a timing one. I would reconsider if colleagues show those results hold under modern identification standards.

responses.point: Hassler (chair) prefers B006 but calls Katz the weaker fit for a trade-shock-centred citation. He would accept a Dorn-for-Katz substitution if the committee decides the trade-shock evidence is the core. He keeps B007 as his first alternative.
responses.response: This is the point on which I could move, so I state my condition. If the committee decides the achievement is specifically the import-competition design, Autor, Dorn and Hanson is the more precise credit and I would accept it. I do not read the achievement that way. The citation I propose is about labour demand and wage structure as well as local adjustment, and that scope needs Katz. I do not want the choice to turn on seniority or on the three-name limit. It should turn on what the citation claims. I agree with your handling of the 2023 and 2024 prizes: they are adjacent in theme, and neither recognised the local-labour-market evidence on trade exposure.

responses.point: Andersson moved from B004 to B006. He argues that one citation can hold both the technology and trade strands if it is framed around labour-demand adjustment, and that the citation should not claim to have originated the task model.
responses.response: I agree with the framing and have adopted it in my wording. I also agree with your reason for moving off B004. Any trio from eight names would write out the estimated and empirical layer that made the framework usable, and the 2021-23 inflation weakens the empirical standing of the Phillips-curve side. I would add one caution to your argument. Saying one citation can hold both strands does not show that the strands are one discovery. The committee should say why they belong together: the same labour-demand question, and the same concern with where adjustment costs fall. Otherwise the wording bundles two prizes under one sentence.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B006 first but calls Katz's marginal claim the most exposed part of the trio, because of his education-technology work with a recent laureate. He names Autor, Dorn and Hanson as the natural fallback within the same discovery.
responses.response: I agree that Katz is the exposed name, and I said so in round 1. I would separate two things in his record. The education-technology race is the part that overlaps with the 2023 prize. The wage-structure and skill-premium evidence is a distinct line, and it is what the B006 citation relies on. I accept your fallback as the right one if the committee cannot agree on that separation. I do not accept that the exposure alone is a reason to drop him. Under that logic the cap decides the prize. I would rather the committee state openly that Dorn's exclusion is a cost of the three-name limit.

responses.point: Krusell moved B006 to first from his opening B007 ranking. He discloses that Persson, credited on B007, is at his home institute, IIES, and he keeps B007 as his first alternative.
responses.response: Your disclosure is noted. I do not adjudicate it, and my own view of B007 does not depend on it. I accept your argument that the formal political-economics programme is distinct from the 2024 institutions prize, and I keep B007 as an alternative for that reason. The merits of B007 and B006 are what separate them for me, so I weigh B007's cleaner credit against B006's design-based identification and wider confirmation, and the second weighs more. I would be uneasy if the choice between them were settled by member ties or support counts, in either direction.

uncertainties: Whether Katz's wage-structure and skill-premium contributions are separable enough from his education-technology work with a recent laureate to carry his marginal credit. If they are not, Autor, Dorn and Hanson becomes the better trio.
Whether the committee treats technology and trade as one discovery (how exposure shifts labour demand and where adjustment costs fall) or two, and whether one citation can say so without bundling.

How persistent and large the China-shock effects are over the long run, whether they generalise beyond the US, and how far shift-share inference concerns qualify the estimates. I treat these as limits on the citation wording, not as grounds for waiting.
How much the 2023 and 2024 prizes reduce the marginal case. I read the overlap as thematic, but I cannot rule out that the committee weighs it for timing.
Whether the B007 position rests on a scientific disagreement over identification or on a preference for cleaner credit. I cannot tell from the round-1 files.
statement.conflict_note: No personal, institutional or co-authorship connection to Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn is apparent from my supplied profile. I disclose field proximity: my research on electrification, labour conflict, railroads and regional change is topically adjacent to B006, and I have tried to hold it to the same criteria as other fields. I am a Lund colleague of Tommy Andersson, and Jan Teorell was formerly at Lund; neither is a candidate, and I note this without adjudicating it. My first-ranked B006 and my alternatives B007 and B001 involve no tie to any credited name on those ballots that is apparent from my profile. I have read colleagues' disclosures (Krusell on Persson and IIES, Friberg, Hassler, Boppart and others) and I do not adjudicate them. I have not independently verified any source claims.
